Data.title: Bitcoin slips as hotter US CPI fuels Fed hike bets
Data.body: The bitcoin price today slipped about 2% on Tuesday, November 10, after hotter-than-expected US consumer price data for October added pressure to cryptocurrencies. What happened to bitcoin price today? Bitcoin last traded at $73,612 at 14:27 GMT, down 2.1% from Monday's close of $75,223. The market was already weaker before the data was released. Bitcoin was near $74,264 at 13:25 GMT, about 1.3% below Monday's close, and dropped to a session low of $73,494 in the five minutes after the data. Ether, XRP and Solana fell further. Ether was at $2,060, down 3.4% from Monday after touching $2,040. XRP was at $1.057, down 3.6%, and Solana at $83.53, down 3.5%. BTC/USD (BTC-USD) 5-minute chart | Source: Yahoo Finance Why is bitcoin falling? Bitcoin price fell after the US inflation data came in higher than expected. The US consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4% in October , against a Dow Jones consensus of 0.3%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Core CPI rose 0.3% against forecasts of 0.2%. The BLS did not publish an annual rate because last year's government shutdown stopped it from collecting October 2025 data. The print fits a risk-off reaction, as firmer rate-hike bets typically weigh on bitcoin. Treasury yields and the dollar jumped. The 10-year yield rose to 4.956% at 14:12 GMT, up from Monday's 4.864%. The 2-year yield had jumped more than 15 basis points to 4.698% shortly after the release. The US dollar index was up 0.4% near 102.01. Fed Governor Christopher Waller, in a speech earlier today , said he was leaning toward a 25 basis point hike in December. But if core CPI came in “around 0.3 percent or even higher,” he said, “a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered.” Institutional flows were already a headwind. US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $201 million of net outflows on Monday, the third straight session of withdrawals, Farside Investors data showed. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust led the redemptions. Outflows over the past seven sessions total about $2.13 billion. What happens next? Traders fully priced in a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting and put the odds of a half-point move at 14.7%, according to CME Group's FedWatch. The Fed held its target range at 3.75%-4.00% in October. Producer price data is due on Friday. US bond markets are closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day, which could thin liquidity. Bitcoin has so far held above $73,000 after the print. Should you buy bitcoin now? Today's drop continues recent weakness rather than standing as a CPI-only crash, with ETF outflows and hike bets already weighing on prices before the data. Data.title: Flare CEO Wants XRP to Break Free From Ripple’s Shadow, XRP Army Reacts
Data.body: The scrutiny surrounding Ripple’s leadership has increased drastically in recent weeks. Hugo Philion, Co-Founder and CEO of Flare Networks, has responded to the recent wave of FUD surrounding XRP and Ripple. BSCN (@BSCNews) shared the CEO’s comments, adding a notable voice to a debate that has grown increasingly heated. Philion’s Case for XRP Independence Philion believes XRP’s future should not depend entirely on Ripple’s decisions. Rather than focusing on price speculation or placing the burden of XRP’s success on Ripple’s executive team, he wants the community to concentrate on finding practical use cases for idle XRP . In his view, there is more to be done for the token than waiting on Ripple to deliver a price outcome. The post arrives as Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse and CTO Emeritus David Schwartz face mounting pressure from XRP holders frustrated by the gap between Ripple’s business growth and XRP’s price performance. Garlinghouse has publicly called XRP Ripple’s North Star , while Schwartz has defended the company’s long-term institutional strategy. Neither response has fully satisfied a community watching XRP trade over 70% below its all-time high. Flare CEO Wants XRP to Break Free From Ripple's Shadow Flare ( @FlareNetworks ) flare-networks:native CEO Hugo Philion ( @HugoPhilion ) has pushed back against recent FUD surrounding $XRP . He argues the token's future should not depend entirely on Ripple's decisions. Instead,… pic.twitter.com/OtTgYTevii — BSCN (@BSCNews) November 9, 2026 What the Community is Saying The reaction to Philion’s post revealed divided sentiment. One response pushed back firmly, arguing that XRP’s value absolutely should depend on Ripple, since that is the foundational premise investors accepted when buying in. He called the idea of investors finding their own return pathways the “stupidest thing I have heard to date.” Another took a more measured view, acknowledging that Philion’s desire for separation could allow XRP to chart its own course, but questioning how sustainable that would be without the infrastructure and support Ripple provides. One reply cut straight to the structural reality, noting that Ripple owns the majority of XRP’s supply. This makes true independence a complicated proposition. Another commenter pointed out that prioritizing utility over speculation is the only way digital assets survive for long. The Bigger Picture Philion’s comments arrive at a tense moment for XRP holders. Ripple continues to expand into stablecoins and institutional products, and community frustration is growing as some believe the company will replace XRP with RLUSD . Many are questioning whether its efforts will ever translate into price performance, but Philion is not criticizing Ripple directly. He is making a case for a more self-sufficient XRP ecosystem where utility drives value rather than corporate decisions alone. Data.title: Valour Lists Eight New Crypto ETPs Including Canton, Morpho and Raydium
Data.body: TL;DR: Valour, a subsidiary of DeFi Technologies, says it has added eight digital asset exchange-traded products to Sweden's Spotlight Stock Market. The November 5 announcement expands the issuer's range beyond the most established cryptocurrencies into a mixture of decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and speculative community tokens. Valour, a subsidiary of DeFi Technologies, says it has added eight digital asset exchange-traded products to Sweden's Spotlight Stock Market. The November 5 announcement expands the issuer's range beyond the most established cryptocurrencies into a mixture of decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and speculative community tokens. The listings widen the menu available through a securities-market wrapper, but the variety also makes it important for investors to understand what each product actually tracks. The eight underlying assets Valour's new SEK-denominated products reference Venice Token (VVV), Canton Coin (CC), Raydium (RAY), Morpho (MORPHO), Maple (SYRUP), Pump.fun (PUMP), Dogwifhat (WIF) and Bonk (BONK). They represent very different markets. Some connect to lending, trading or institutional blockchain networks, while others derive demand from online communities and token speculation. Presenting all eight as one diversified crypto strategy would be misleading. A buyer of one listed product is exposed to its specific token and to the terms of the ETP, not to a balanced basket of the eight assets. Why the wrapper matters An exchange-traded product can give eligible investors exposure through a brokerage account rather than requiring them to maintain a wallet and manage token transfers. That can simplify record keeping and access within markets where the product is available. It does not necessarily provide the same legal structure or protections as a conventional equity fund, however. Investors should review whether the product is physically backed, how custody is handled, what fees are charged, and whether creation and redemption work efficiently. The securities wrapper can reduce some operational burdens while leaving underlying crypto price risk very much intact. A wide spectrum of token risks Canton and Morpho are associated with institutional blockchain and DeFi infrastructure, Raydium with Solana-based trading and Maple with onchain credit. By contrast, meme-linked tokens such as Dogwifhat and Bonk have historically depended heavily on market sentiment. Pump.fun exposure carries its own commercial and regulatory questions. None of these classifications determines future performance, but the differences matter for portfolio construction and due diligence. The existence of a regulated trading venue for an ETP is not an official endorsement of the underlying token's economic value. Trading in Swedish kronor adds another consideration The products are quoted in SEK, so an investor whose reference currency is different must consider exchange-rate moves as well as the token price. Trading hours and liquidity may also differ from around-the-clock cryptocurrency markets. That mismatch can create wider spreads or price gaps when significant token moves occur while the securities venue is closed. Buyers should examine the issuer's market-making arrangements and the gap between quoted prices and indicative net asset values rather than assuming that an exchange listing always guarantees a tight execution price. A useful signal, with limits Valour's expansion shows how issuers are testing demand for more specialized crypto exposures through familiar financial channels. Whether the new products become meaningful investment options will depend on trading volumes, spreads, fees, custody disclosures and sustained interest beyond launch week. For market observers, the story is less about eight fresh tickers than the effort to package increasingly niche digital assets for traditional securities accounts—and the safeguards needed when investors follow them there. Primary source: DeFi Technologies / Valour product announcement . For additional context, see NewsBTC’s analysis of trading flows through established Bitcoin funds . This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Data.title: Attention iPhone Users! Binance Warns: “Your Bitcoin and Altcoins May Be at Risk!”
Data.body: Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has issued a new warning as it tries to recover from the $6.3 billion hack it suffered at the end of October. At this point, Binance warned iPhone users about a security vulnerability called “worse_query” affecting iOS versions 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2. This security vulnerability could allow malicious applications to access files belonging to other applications. Cryptocurrency Wallets May Be at Risk! Binance, in a statement, drew attention to a security vulnerability affecting iOS versions 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2, and warned iPhone users against potential cryptocurrency theft. This vulnerability allows malicious applications to access and read local files of other applications that they would not normally have access to. According to Binance, this also creates the risk of obtaining cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases, private keys, and login credentials that are stored unprotected on devices. At this point, Binance emphasized that the problem was not unique to its platform, but directly related to the security mechanisms of the iOS operating system. Binance Offers Security Advice to Users! The exchange advised users to remove applications downloaded from untrusted sources, especially those installed via sideloading or manually signed IPA files. He also recommended using the latest official versions of iOS and all applications. He suggested deleting applications downloaded from untrusted sources, including iOS, and updating iOS and all applications to the latest official versions. Users who suspect a security breach were advised to create a new wallet on a clean, virus-free device, transfer their assets to this wallet, and reset their active login sessions. Binance also added that they have not encountered any verified cases where crypto wallets were accessed or funds were stolen using this vulnerability. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Apple and Google push iOS and Chrome updates as crypto wallet attacks pile up
Data.body: iPhone and Chrome browser users got new updates on the same day as Apple and Google moved to plug security vulnerabilities on two of the most popular platforms among crypto users. The updates, which landed on the same day by coincidence, are the latest security patches to be applied in a year where exploit kits and wallet drainers have consistently targeted crypto users’ devices. Google fixes zero-day vulnerability in Chrome According to the Chrome Releases blog , Google pushed through nine security fixes in its latest update for Windows, Mac and Linux. One of the flaws that Google fixed, CVE-2026-125350, was already being exploited. The company conceded that fact in a November 6 response to an anonymous report, writing that it “is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild.” The security update will roll out to users over the next few days, with some reaching users over the next few weeks. Google urged Chrome users to restart their browsers, as most browsers update at launch. Has Apple released a new iPhone update? iPhone users with iPhone 11 or later received iOS 27.2.1 on November 9. Apple also released iPadOS 27.2.1 for the iPad on the same day. The patch fixes flaws in Messages, Bluetooth and App Intents, including one (CVE-2026-113961) that could allow an attacker to remotely join and read chats on iMessage groups. Another flaw in App Intents, CVE-2026-113963, could allow attackers to access sensitive user information. None of the flaws that Apple fixed have been described as exploited in the wild, unlike in the Chrome case. Notably, Apple’s support pages clarify that the iPhone maker does not disclose the details of a flaw until it ships a fix. Attackers are targeting crypto users with exploits The patches that Google and Apple published carry major stakes for crypto holders who have been under siege this year. Attackers have been using the DarkSword exploit chain to steal information from cryptocurrency wallet apps and other personal data since at least November 2025. The flaw disclosed by Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) in March spread to iPhones running iOS 18.4 through 18.7 using six vulnerabilities. A Censys report found servers pairing DarkSword and Coruna to steal data and recovery phrases from wallet apps like Coinbase, MetaMask, OKEx, Phantom and Trust Wallet as of early October. The update to iOS 26.3 plugged the hold that DarkSword attackers were exploiting. Attackers are consistently building exploit routes to reach crypto users even while developers are fixing existing software flaws. One of them, found by SlowMist and OKX, implicated the FomoPeek iOS app in the theft of roughly $580,000 in crypto. A supply chain incident on Trust Wallet led to losses of more than $6 million in December 2025, as Cryptopolitan reported at the time. In a November 6 blog , Trust Wallet told iPhone owners, especially those who have not updated to version iOS 18.7, to install the latest iOS. The wallet provider also advised iPhone users to update, turn on Lockdown Mode if an update is not possible, and ensure not to store recovery phrases as photos or on notes apps, as exploits are already known to look for such files on their devices. Data.title: Bitcoin Price Analysis: Will BTC Crash Below $70K Next as Selling Pressure Intensifies?
Data.body: Bitcoin has slipped beneath the $74K support area, leaving buyers struggling to regain control near $74.5K. The latest breakdown increases the risk of a deeper correction, while the liquidation heatmap highlights nearby concentrations on both sides of the market. Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart The daily chart shows Bitcoin trading below the lower boundary of the $75K–$78K demand zone following repeated tests. The earlier recovery toward $81K was rejected near the ascending channel’s midpoint, and subsequent rebounds have failed to reverse the sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Although recent candles show buying interest beneath $74K, the response has been insufficient to reclaim the broken demand zone sustainably. The current daily candle remains open, so confirmation depends on whether Bitcoin closes below $75K or recovers that level before the session ends. Continued acceptance beneath $75K would leave the ascending channel’s lower boundary, around $73K, as the next important technical reference. A decisive break below that trendline would weaken the broader rising structure and expose the marked $67.8K–$69.8K demand zone, which encompasses part of August’s strong upward expansion. Alternatively, reclaiming $75K would reduce immediate downside pressure, but buyers would still need to recover $78K to demonstrate a more meaningful improvement. Until then, rebounds remain vulnerable to selling within the former demand area. BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart The four-hour chart shows Bitcoin breaking beneath both its descending channel’s lower boundary and the recent consolidation base. The marked decision zone around $75.5K–$77K now sits overhead, making it an important test for any recovery. The initial selloff reached approximately $73.5K before buyers pushed the price back toward $75.5K. However, that bounce failed near the lower edge of the decision zone, and BTC has since returned toward $74.5K. This rejection suggests that former support is beginning to act as resistance. As long as Bitcoin remains below $75.5K–$77K, another test of the $73.5K low remains plausible. Losing that low would reinforce the bearish continuation scenario and bring the daily channel support around $73K into focus. Conversely, reclaiming the decision zone would weaken the immediate breakdown and could support a recovery toward the descending channel’s upper boundary around $79K–$80K. The broader $79.8K–$82K supply zone remains a substantial obstacle beyond that initial recovery. Sentiment Analysis The Binance liquidation heatmap shows a nearby concentration of estimated long-liquidation exposure around $73K–$73.5K, beneath Bitcoin’s current price. This broadly aligns with the recent low and the approaching daily channel boundary, making it a relevant area if selling continues. A move through this concentration could trigger forced long closures and amplify short-term volatility. However, the cluster represents potential liquidation exposure rather than confirmed buying demand, so reaching it would not automatically establish a bottom. Above the market, a prominent concentration sits around $76.5K–$77.5K, overlapping the upper portion of the four-hour decision zone. A successful reclaim of nearby resistance could expose these levels and potentially accelerate a rebound through short liquidations. Larger overhead concentrations remain around $81K–$82K. For now, the weak price structure keeps the nearby downside cluster in focus. A sustained recovery through $75.5K–$77K would be needed to shift attention toward the more substantial liquidation concentrations above. Data.title: US inflation runs hotter than expected at 0.4% in October
Data.body: US inflation came in hotter than expected at 0.4% in October, giving Wall Street another reason to worry about the Federal Reserve raising interest rates again. The latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report showed that Americans paid more for groceries, housing, electricity, insurance, and healthcare. September was worse, with prices climbing 0.6%, but the slowdown hasn’t exactly made inflation disappear. It makes things especially awkward for the Federal Reserve. At the October meeting, they voted 10 to 2 to keep interest rates in the 3.75% to 4% range, deciding to get some more data on the economy before deciding again. An interest rate rise is not assured, but rising prices could complicate things. Food and housing prices keep inflation painfully high Housing was responsible for a considerable chunk of October’s inflation. Rent, homeownership costs, and hotel stays all became more expensive, with shelter accounting for over 30% of the overall monthly increase. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said, “The shelter index increased 0.3 percent over the month after rising 0.4 percent in September. The index for owners’ equivalent rent rose 0.3 percent in October, and the index for rent increased 0.2 percent. The lodging away from home index rose 0.6 percent in October after rising 2.0 percent the previous month.” Grocery shopping wasn’t much better. Food prices started climbing again after taking a break the previous month, with several everyday items becoming noticeably more expensive. “The food index rose 0.5 percent in October after being unchanged in September. The food at home index increased 0.4 percent over the month. Four of the six major grocery store food group indexes increased in October, while one index decreased,” the BLS said. Snacks jumped 1%, beef increased 0.9%, and the broader category covering meat, poultry, fish, and eggs rose 0.5%. Fruits, vegetables, and dairy products each became 0.6% more expensive. Other groceries climbed 0.7%. Energy inflation was also positive, though much lower than before. The price index grew by 0.7% after increasing by 5.2% in September. The gasoline price index rose by 1% after growing by 9.1% the previous month. The fuel oil price index increased by 2%, while the electricity index increased by 0.9%. Natural gas service was cheaper, falling 0.8%, while energy services increased 0.6%. Before seasonal adjustments, gasoline prices actually declined 0.7%. Core inflation refuses to cool as Wall Street watches the Fed Meanwhile, core CPI increased 0.3% for the third consecutive month, suggesting price pressures remain widespread. Recreation was among the biggest contributors, alongside insurance and other household expenses. “The index for recreation increased 0.8 percent over the month after rising 0.5 percent in September. The motor vehicle insurance index rose 0.7 percent in October, and the household furnishings and operations index increased 0.2 percent,” the BLS said. Transportation services increased 0.8%, education gained 0.3%, and new vehicles became 0.2% more expensive. Apparel, airline fares, and personal care also recorded increases. Healthcare bills kept climbing, too. Medical care inflation reached 0.3%, compared with 0.1% in September. Hospital services rose 0.8%, physicians’ services gained 0.4%, and prescription drugs increased 0.3%. Medical care commodities advanced 0.5%. Used cars offered one of the few meaningful price declines. “The index for used cars and trucks declined 1.2 percent in October after rising 0.7 percent in September. The communication index decreased 0.1 percent over the month,” the BLS said. The broader CPI-U reached 337.511, increasing 0.2% before seasonal adjustment. The CPI-W, covering urban wage earners and clerical workers, reached 331.147 after gaining 0.1%. The chained CPI rose 0.2%, with recent readings still subject to revision. Annual comparisons remain incomplete because the 2025 government funding lapse prevented October data collection. Available figures showed gasoline prices up 37.4% from a year earlier, new vehicles gaining 0.7%, and used vehicles falling 3.3%. For investors, the immediate concern is whether the Fed will interpret October’s figures as another warning that inflation is proving harder to control than expected. Don’t just read crypto news. Data.title: Two Covered Call ETFs To Dump Before They Destroy Your Wealth
Data.body: Summary Today's market conditions strongly favour covered call ETFs as an income strategy. Yet some option income structures become more dangerous, not safer, as volatility rises. In this article, I share two examples, each with its own structural flaw that eats away at shareholder value. Despite their eye-catching yields, I think both carry a serious risk of permanent capital loss. The current market conditions are extremely favorable for covered call ETFs. With perhaps a few exceptions, most asset classes that are higher in the risk curve than the risk-free instruments ( SGOV ) face a material risk of being repriced to the downside. One thing is the AI ( QQQ ) and private credit ( BIZD ), but we are also talking about durable investments such as MLPs via the Alerian MLP ETF ( AMLP ), REITs via the Vanguard Real Estate ETF ( VNQ ), and infrastructure, as proxied by the Reaves Utility Income Fund ( UTG ) that are subject to a serious downside risk. Sure, the drivers may differ. For MLPs it is the potential solution in Iran and the lower oil price. For REITs and infrastructure, it is rising inflation and an upwards shift in the interest rate curve. For AI it is a combination of excessive multiples , a debt-driven CapEx cycle, and a series of practical headwinds on the ground. In general, when the odds of a downside exceed those for the upside, a covered call ETF lever is the right one to pull. This is because if the underlying assets that are subject to an option income strategy remain range-bound or decline, the option premiums can be easily pocketed without any opportunity cost. These proceeds can contribute to excess returns. On top of that, the higher volatility is directly beneficial to the option premiums. Namely, an option income vehicle gets a bigger bang for the buck when writing specific contracts or creating option strategies. Furthermore, the increase of the premium amount raises the bar higher that the underlying asset has to surpass in order to inflict damage in terms of an opportunity cost (i.e., the ETF not participating in the upside rally). That said, as I articulated in my recent piece that was a strategic one: there are certain covered call ETFs and option income vehicle categories that actually become more dangerous in these kinds of conditions. More specifically, I'm talking about single security-based covered call ETFs and zero-day expiration or 0DTE vehicles—primarily because of their heightened upside capping risks. In this article, I thought that it could be interesting to issue a more practical piece, elaborating on two concrete option income ETFs, which, in my humble opinion, carry a significant risk of shareholder wealth destruction. Each of them has a different spin from each other and the substance that I shared in my previous article. #1: The YieldMax Ultra Option Income Strategy ETF, 93% The YieldMax Ultra Option Income Strategy ETF ( ULTY ) is a concentrated, high-income, and weekly-paying ETF. The way ULTY captures premiums and accommodates its monstrous yield is the following: Buys 15-30 US stocks based on the highest implied volatility levels. In practice, it boils down to stocks where the market expects big price swings or they are just before big events such as earnings releases, mergers, etc. On these names which can be bought either synthetically (via specific option positions) or physically (outright acquisitions), ULTY applies various option strategies. Here the management has almost full flexibility to construct whatever option exposure they deem fit—e.g., covered calls, put spreads, collars, etc. Take a look at the chart below to see what fruit ULTY's strategy has borne: YCharts I have compared it to the Goldman Sachs Nasdaq-100 Premium Income ETF ( GPIQ ), which is also a volatility-biased option income ETF, as it sells calls against inherently volatile AI names (in this case the QQQ index). The NAV erosion has been staggering. The total returns have been unacceptable. And the pace of a dividend decline has been mind-boggling: YCharts Now, the main reason behind this is the bias towards the highest implied vol against which an option income overlay is assigned. Namely, what ULTY does is it caps the upside potential of exactly the names that have the potential to explode higher and deliver exceptional returns. Additionally, it dedicates part of the collected premiums for downside protection on an individual stock level. Hedging the downside for an extremely volatile stock is quite expensive. In the chart below, you can see my calculus based on the November 9 holdings list. ULTY has effectively created a collar, which on a portfolio-wide basis translates to the following pay-off profile: Created by the author (YieldMax) In other words, ULTY's collar limits losses to 7.8% of NAV but caps gains at 5.6%. If we look at some of the biggest ULTY's holdings , such as Analog Devices, Inc. ( ADI ), Shopify Inc. ( SHOP ), and Lam Research Corporation ( LRCX ). We can see that many of them are very volatile, experiencing swings that greatly exceed the -5.6% to +7.8% range. YCharts In a nutshell, ULTY's collar caps the upside of precisely those high-vol names that tend to deliver outsized rallies. On top of this, ULTY pays for costly stock-level hedges that keep eating into the collected premiums. Given the current elevated volatility environment, I think that it is very likely that we see an accelerated ULTY's NAV and distribution erosion. #2: The NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF, 31% The NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF ( BTCI ) is a similar problem-option-income ETF (but perhaps the issue here is not as drastic as for ULTY). BTCI is a covered call ETF vehicle, which sells out-of-the-money calls against physically (directly) owned bitcoin ETFs—the VanEck Bitcoin ETF ( HODL ) and the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF ( IBIT ). So, at its core, BTCI functions just as any conventional covered call ETF vehicle. Yet there are a couple of critical nuances—all of which make the investment case unacceptable and tilted towards a huge loss of capital. Let's start with two charts, just to set the scene. In the past year or so, BTCI has lost ~43% of its NAV and, with dividends included, registered a negative total return of 26%. YCharts And as it is usually the case with plunging covered call ETFs, the dividends tend to follow in the same direction: Seeking Alpha I think that you will agree with me that BTCI as a covered call ETF has provided no protection whatsoever against the meltdown in bitcoin. On a total return basis, the results (at least in this year) have been almost identical. Yet BTCI is in a disadvantageous position relative to the pure-play bitcoin holding and, more importantly, as a stand-alone investment. Three things. First, although BTCI's overwrite is 45% of the total NAV, it still faces a significant opportunity cost and thus a structural NAV drag compared to the physical holding. Based on the current holdings list, we can calculate that, say, if IBIT rises by ~30% (until December 18), then BTCI would give up about 8.5% of NAV. At this point in time, it might sound totally unrealistic to see IBIT surge this high. So, this leads me to the second point. Second, we have to understand that bitcoin is a high-beta asset class. The chart below depicts the rolling 3-year beta of bitcoin to the S&P 500 ( SPY ). FMR LLC So, if we believe that the stock market is likely to head downwards and the recent pullback was just the first signs of a more notable correction, then we have to be ready to see quite a violent move in bitcoin as well. And let's not forget that the crypto world has fallen under significant pressure amid the political changes and overall de-risking in the system. In such a scenario, BTCI's partial overwrite would offer only a thin premium cushion, while the ETF would still absorb the bulk of drawdown in IBIT. Third, and perhaps most importantly, once the current option contracts expire, BTCI will have to roll them into new ones against a much lower IBIT price. Namely, the new cost basis is very likely to get locked in at the depressed level, which means that the new strikes will sit closer to the current price and introduce a tighter upside cap. So what this means is that even if bitcoin experiences a sharp recovery (say, quite close to the previous highs), BTCI would only participate in a fraction of it, thereby turning a temporary drawdown into a permanent NAV impairment (or drag). All in all, BTCI is just like ULTY in essence that in the current vol regime, a very juicy yield can easily come at the price of a structural and permanent shareholder wealth destruction.

Data.title: Backed by $80 Million, Alta is Building the Infrastructure to Bring Global Banking Onchain
Data.body: San Francisco, CA, USA, November 10th, 2026, Chainwire New funding will advance institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure built for privacy, compliance, and global connectivity Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, today announced it has raised $80 million in total funding, including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49. Alta is building new institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that enables financial assets and products to move instantly, globally, and programmatically. Unlike existing infrastructure built primarily for crypto-native applications, Alta is designed to meet the privacy, compliance, neutrality, and operational requirements of regulated financial institutions while supporting transactions across assets, chains, and jurisdictions. Its launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates. “Existing blockchains aren’t designed for the privacy and compliance requirements of global financial institutions,” said Loong Wang, Co-Founder and CEO of Alta. “We're taking a fundamentally different approach, building privacy, programmable compliance, and identity and authorization directly into the blockchain. This will enable money and assets to move instantly, globally, and securely, whether it's a bank settling a transaction or an AI agent making a payment.” Today's global financial system is fragmented and still has many areas of inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must maintain substantial cash buffers to ensure liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. An estimated $4 trillion is tied up in prefunded accounts globally. Alta is building a more efficient system, combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management capabilities. At the core of Alta's technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It enables institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private while verifying that transactions meet the required rules. Designed to work across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta combines programmable compliance with the controls and scalability needed for institutional finance and agentic commerce. “Technology alone won't be enough to modernize global finance. Financial institutions need infrastructure they can trust, with clear controls over who they're transacting with, where money can move, and how sensitive information is protected,” said Catherine Porter, Co-Founder and President of Alta. “As AI agents increasingly make financial decisions and execute transactions, that trust becomes even more critical. Privacy, compliance, and accountability just aren’t barriers to innovation – they’re what will allow it to scale.” Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. In addition to pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies. Alta is designed as neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can build on. Alta’s first product will help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and reduce cash buffers tied up in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it will enable just-in-time funding, more efficient foreign exchange, and allow businesses to instantly move in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital. “With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.” Backed by Leading Global Investors Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation. “Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures. “The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV. The new funding will support continued development of Alta's blockchain infrastructure, expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and growth of its engineering and compliance teams. About Alta Alta is building global financial infrastructure for the future of tokenized finance. Combining an institutional-grade blockchain with global payments connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury capabilities, Alta is creating the foundation for a more efficient, private, compliant, and connected global financial system. Data.title: Anthropic to raise up to $64 billion from IPO , targets $1 trillion valuation
Data.body: Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion as it prepares to go public. The company behind Claude hopes to raise up to $64.4 billion, according to a filing with the U.S. SEC. The listing will give public investors their first chance to see how much a major AI company is worth. The numbers behind the offering Anthropic and some of its existing investors are selling shares for $70 to $78 each , according to the SEC filing. The company is offering 801.4 million shares, while its investors are selling another 23.6 million. This brings the total number of shares on offer to 825 million. Anthropic is also raising $26 billion from private investors. This could take its total fundraising to $90.4 billion, according to Reuters. The deal would rank among the biggest fundraising efforts in the tech industry. Anthropic has changed its fundraising target several times. An earlier draft showed that the company planned to raise up to $69.3 billion from the public sale. The company, however, later lowered the target to $64.4 billion. The Globe and Mail added that the company shared the deal terms with investment banks before withdrawing them late on November 9. Companies involved in Anthropic’s IPO Major tech companies are backing Anthropic’s private share sale. Google’s parent Alphabet, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) are a part of the AI giant’s financial backers. These also include Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley will be leading the banks in charge of the offering. Once the IPO is complete, Anthropic’s shares will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT.” Growth outruns doubts Anthropic’s revenue grew 47% to $16.96 billion in the third quarter. This was slower than the 144% growth recorded in the previous quarter. The company’s net loss also saw a drop. The Financial Times reported that Anthropic’s annual revenue rate reached $81 billion in October, up $10 billion from September. The company said more people are using Claude, including its tools for health care, finance and legal services. Anthropic is also facing huge costs. The company has about $900 billion in computing deals with Amazon, Google and other partners. Some of this spending is dependent on external funding. In its prospectus, Anthropic said it hopes to “bring forth an age of miracles” but also warned that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Investors more cautious about AI The timing may also work against Anthropic. The Nasdaq recorded its biggest one-day fall in 19 months on November 5. The decline followed growing concerns that Democrats’ gains in the US midterm elections could lead to tighter rules for the construction of data centers. The Financial Times noted that Democrats have pledged to slow data center expansion. Anthropic’s target value is still below SpaceX’s. Elon Musk’s company went public in June with a $1.78 trillion valuation while raising $86 billion. Anthropic’s $1.4 trillion target is also lower than earlier estimates of nearly $2 trillion. The company was last valued at $965 billion in a private funding round in May. Anthropic’s backers are hoping more investors will buy its shares, the Financial Times reported. These include index funds and large investment firms that do not yet own the stock but may have to buy it once Anthropic joins major market indexes. Don’t just read crypto news. Understand it. Data.title: Nvidia Stock: BofA Drops NVDA From Top Picks as Wells Fargo Cuts Price Target to $300
Data.body: Key takeaways Bank of America removes Nvidia from its highest-conviction list Wells Fargo cuts Nvidia's price target from $315 to $300 Both banks maintain bullish ratings despite growing uncertainty Nvidia ( NASDAQ: NVDA ) is facing renewed scrutiny from Wall Street after Bank of America removed the chipmaker from its highest-conviction stock list, while Wells Fargo reduced its price target to $300 from $315 amid concerns about leadership uncertainty. The November 10 decisions follow a difficult trading session in which NVDA fell 4.27% to $178.67, extending its recent decline even as other technology stocks recovered. However, neither bank abandoned its bullish outlook. Bank of America maintained its Buy rating and $350 price target, while Wells Fargo retained an Overweight rating, highlighting a growing distinction between Nvidia's long-term earnings potential and immediate investment risks. Bank of America Removes Nvidia, Micron and Lam Research Bank of America removed Nvidia, Micron Technology (MU) and Lam Research (LRCX) from its US 1 List, which consists of selected investment ideas drawn from the bank's Buy-rated US stocks. All three chipmakers retained their Buy ratings, meaning the change represents a reduction in their preferred-list status rather than a formal downgrade. The bank did not publicly disclose a specific reason for the removals in the available reporting. The decision follows a sharp semiconductor valuation reset , during which investors reduced the earnings multiples they were willing to pay despite continued demand for advanced computing infrastructure. Bank of America's semiconductor research indicates that the sector has experienced an approximately 37% correction, leaving chip stocks trading near 13.7 times forward earnings. That represents a roughly 22% discount to the broader S&P 500, reflecting the technology sector's declining valuation premium . Wells Fargo Cuts Nvidia Target as Leadership Risks Grow Wells Fargo separately lowered its Nvidia price target by approximately 4.8%, from $315 to $300, citing uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang and the potential consequences of ongoing investigations. The decision follows Nvidia's November 8 board announcement confirming an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company emphasized that it had no reason to believe its confidential information or US national security had been compromised. The board's review adds uncertainty following the recent NVDA stock selloff , when Nvidia declined despite gains across other major technology companies. Nevertheless, Wells Fargo maintained its Overweight rating and expects continued growth in Nvidia's AI infrastructure business. Its revised $300 target still implies approximately 68% upside from Nvidia's November 9 closing price, while Bank of America's $350 objective implies nearly 96%. Nvidia Earnings Could Determine the Next Major Move The conflicting signals arrive ahead of Nvidia's November 17 fiscal third-quarter earnings announcement. In its previous earnings release , Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion, more than double the previous year's figure, including $89 billion from data centers. The company projected approximately $108 billion in third-quarter revenue, underscoring the scale of demand for AI computing. Still, investors are increasingly concerned about China chip restrictions and whether customers can sustain their enormous infrastructure spending commitments. Broader weakness in AI stocks has also made investors more sensitive to risks that previously received less attention.

Data.title: Address poisoners target a 2015 genesis Ethereum wallet minutes after its test payment
Data.body: Just under 3 minutes after an Ethereum wallet from the network’s 2015 genesis block sent funds for the first time in 11 years, scammers started spraying dust at it. The owner moved 2,154.94 ETH, worth some $4.6 million at the time, to the right place, disregarding the lookalike addresses. Two lookalikes ending in 1A44 copied the new recipient The address first obtained ether in Ethereum’s genesis block in July 2015, and another 755 ETH in March 2016. It didn’t send anything until late Monday, when it fired off a $106 test payment of 0.05 ETH at 22:04 UTC. Whale Alert flagged the transaction as a dormant pre-mine address with 2,155 ETH that has been active again after 11.3 years. Whale Alert flags the dormant pre-mine address waking after 11.3 years, posted by @whale_alert on X late on November 9, 2026, UTC. The test moved to a new address starting 0x1321beb8 and ending 1A44. Within three minutes, the old wallet started to receive small amounts of ETH from two addresses contrived to look like that recipient. First one starts at 0x13211f, the other at 0x1321FB. Both finish at 1A44. Both lookalikes were financed by accounts labeled as “Fake_Phishing” by Etherscan. The busier lookalike sent 43 payments of dust to the genesis wallet . Owner sent 2,154.94 ETH to the right address 38 minutes later At 22:20 UTC the new wallet sent out 0.01 ETH and almost all of it returned three minutes later. 38 minutes after the first test, at 22:42 UTC, the old wallet sent the full 2,154.94 ETH to the correct address 0x1321beb8. The genesis wallet now has about 0.0004 ETH and the recipient has about 2,155 ETH. The 0x1321FB lookalike sent again at 23:03 UTC and a third lookalike ending in 1A44 sent zero-value transfers at 03:36 and 03:49 UTC on Tuesday. Address poisoning takes advantage of how wallets truncate long addresses. Instead of showing all 42 characters, a wallet displays something like 0x6D90…2E48. Attackers churn through millions of vanity addresses until one matches the first and last characters of a target’s real contact. They then send dust or a zero-value transaction which slots the fake address into the victim’s recent history. If the user copies it for the next payment, they send the money to the attacker. Ethereum transfers cannot be reversed. In December 2025, a trader lost around $50 million in USDT after a script poisoned the history right after a $50 test transaction. In January 2026, a victim sent 4,556 ETH ($12.25 million) to an address controlled by an attacker. Another victim lost $600,000 in February. According to Cryptopolitan , there are over a million poisoning attempts on Ethereum each day. In January, Citi warned that spam was amplifying Ethereum’s record transaction numbers, with most of the transfers worth less than $1. The smartest crypto minds already read our newsletter. Want in? Join them .
